To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
locked in ALS patients were able to reach and grasp a glass of water through a humanoid robot controlled by a brain computer interface.

1) locked in ALS patients are able to control a humanoid robot through a BCI system, 2) the humanoid robot can successfully execute a task that requires the robot to reach and grasp a glass of water, 3) the robot can be trained to recognize different environmental conditions (e.g., different colors of the glass), 4) the robot can successfully execute the task in different environmental conditions, 5) healthy subjects can also use this system to successfully execute the task.

a BCI system can be used to directly control a humanoid robot, and that ALS patients with complete paralysis of the limbs and the vocal tract can successfully use this BCI controlled humanoid to reach and grasp an object.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a BCI based robotic interface that allows ALS patients to control a humanoid robot and to perform basic tasks.
the development and evaluation of a BCI controlled humanoid robot for reaching and grasping objects by locked in ALS subjects.
the development of a BCI operated humanoid robot for locked in patients, with the aim of providing a new way of communication and control of the surrounding environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
BCI operated robotic systems can be used to improve the quality of life of locked in ALS patients.
the use of a humanoid robot operated through a P300 BCI system can be considered an effective way to allow ALS patients to reach, grasp and drink from a glass of water.
BCI technology may provide locked in ALS patients with a new way to regain control of the world around them.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of BCI operated robots may allow patients to perform tasks they could not perform anymore, such as reaching and grasping an object, or even moving in a wheelchair.
BCI technology can be a useful tool for ALS patients to improve their quality of life.
BCI technology is now mature enough to be used by ALS patients to control robots for basic communication and environmental interaction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of humanoid robots controlled by BCI may represent a new approach to assist locked in patients with ALS in the daily living.
locked in ALS patients could be able to perform basic daily activities through the use of an artificial body.
BCI operated humanoid robots can be used to help ALS patients in daily activities.
